title: Add data privacy statement
body:
We want to implement eLabFTW at our university and need to take care of data privacy. The requested feature would be an optional additional page before the actual registration with the data privacy statement. Ideally, the following requirements are met:

* activate optional data privacy statement from system admin panel, similar to enabling account creation 
* add a field where an individual data privacy statement can be entered, e.g. with markdown or html format
* the privacy statement has to be explicitly approved, e.g. with a button press on a page before or via checking a box
* after successful registration the data privacy statement is mailed to the user and preferably, has to be confirmed again upon confirming the mail adress (i.e. double opt-in)
* add an optional additional link to the data privacy statement of the institution, a good position would be in the footer of the page where the links for admin pages are - currently, this can be achieved by exchanging the documentation link from the admin panel 

Thanks
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Hello,

Thanks for the suggestion, indeed it is something that should be added. I have a question: is the double opt-in really necessary? Do you have an authoritative source for what really needs to be implemented?

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
We were discussing this issue with our data privacy officer. According to him, a double opt-in would be the best case scenario to have a double validation. However, a single opt-in upon registration i.e. "If you continue with the registration you agree to the above terms" with a confirmation e.g. via button-press or checking a box is sufficient. In any case, the confirmation has to be saved with the data privacy statement, ideally in a printable form to be archived locally.
But I can ask the specific requirements in these regards, ideally with a link to an official site.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: Yes if you can be very specific it would help a lot. On my side I'll go ask if we have a Data privacy officer here in Curie :)

comments.author: Participant 1
Participant 3
comments.body: I'll second the request for the privacy page. For integration into our identity federation, they require a privacy statement (PDF or HTML page). From our understanding, for scientific data integrity, the user cannot request to delete all information associated with them and instead must ask individually from each group administrator if they wish to delete data that is in an experiment. Otherwise, it would be like someone from the university taking scissors to a physical lab notebook.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: I'll let you know on this issue how I plan to implement it so we can discuss it before complete integration.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
We were discussing data privacy in terms of scientific data at our insitute as well. According to our data privacy officer, it can be requested to delete personal information, i.e. mail address and telefone number along with other information visible on the team tab. I agree with @TheGreatFox that a full deletion of all scientific data cannot be requested but it is neither personal nor private data anyway.

Regarding a privacy statement: A default version in elabFTW is definitely a nice to have, but it should be customizable according to specific needs. We are currently waiting for a translation of our universities statement into English that could serve as a template.

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body: Yes, I'll provide an editable template.

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body: We finally received the translation of our privacy statement, we just need to fill out some missing points on what is actually stored by elabFTW. @NicolasCARPi Can you provide a list of information that is logged while using elabFTW? There's the obvious such as email and full name but maybe there are some "hidden" logs such as revisions with name and time which may be connected to [Issue #924](https://github.com/elabftw/elabftw/issues/924).

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Well, in the `users` table, there is the email, firstname, lastname. Then there is phone, cellphone, skype, website, but these are not mandatory fields. Also, I'll probably change them at some point because they are a bit pointless…

Rest of the app is just integers mostly.

There is a anti brute force system, but it logs a hash of the IP + UserAgent, so not identifiable info.

Then there is the nginx webserver in the container that logs the IP address with the time for each requests (in /var/log/nginx/access.log).

> maybe there are some "hidden" logs such as revisions with name and time which may be connected to Issue #924.

This would be a pointer to the users row anyway, so just a number.

comments.author: Participant 4
comments.body: See how another OS project handles this: https://rocket.chat/2018/05/20/gdpr/

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Ok this is now implemented. See commit message:

create a privacy_policy config entry editable by sysadmin
default is null and no checkbox is show upon registration
after edition of the default template, a check box is shown on the
register page with a link to the policy (displayed in the page on click)

![2019-03-13-191126_600x221_scrot](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3043706/54303644-c191ae00-45c3-11e9-82cd-d2313655c2fb.png)

The template can be seen here: https://github.com/elabftw/elabftw/blob/hypernext/src/templates/privacy-policy.html

We will see later if some modifications need to be made for better compliance, but I think as a first step it's pretty good :)

comments.author: Participant 5
comments.body: Hi! Unfortunately, when the team admin adds new users, the privacy policy is never displayed when logging in via Shibboleth and the user never has to agree to it. Is there a variable that can be queried if the user logs in for the first time?

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
>  Is there a variable that can be queried if the user logs in for the first time?

Yes there is `last_login` that is null at first.

Also, I know a service that does the privacy policy step at the IDP level, so maybe that could also be a solution for you: when you login to a service for the first time, you have to accept the terms of use for that service.

scope: Current retrievable issue body and issue comments; not the original study's historical snapshot. Linked pages and attachments are not fetched.
